reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that tournament efficacy is quantified through inversion count—a metric measuring deviation from true strength rankings. Simulations under six win-probability models (parametric skill gaps and empirical calibrations) show Swiss systems with 5 rounds consistently outperform knockout formats. This dominance is robust across skill levels (1, 5, 10) and sport-specific models (chess, soccer, tennis). The key mathematical structure is a probabilistic ranking recovery framework where each tournament design is evaluated via repeated Monte Carlo trials. The failure mode occurs when seeding is overvalued—realistic seeding improves efficacy by only ~3%, contrary to intuition. The GSE mapping leverages this simulation harness for state transitions in futures markets, while GSI applies inversion count as a Bayesian loss function for calibrated ranking confidence intervals.
